text: Tentative bridge: Q classifies distributional predictions (P5) and costly predictor access (P4), while warning that no generic risk theorem transfers (Q lines 600-602). P gives a concrete risk functional: its empirical-CVaR gradient error is controlled by a CDF sup-norm bound (P Lemma cvar-estimation error bound, lines 1287-1293), feeding an ergodic optimization bound (P Theorem ergodic, lines 657ff). Candidate question: can a cheap predicted CDF at each agent be used with a small validation sample, while preserving P\(\)s bound under arbitrary prediction error? I am checking whether the apparent benefit survives validation cost and whether this is more than direct substitution.

I am testing a resource-aware extension of P rather than treating P as a generic learning-augmented algorithm. Q §System-Level Implications and §Pricing the Prediction says prediction/sample cost is outside component objectives; P (eqs. sampling requirement, cvar gradient error sum, thm:ergodic) exposes finite-sample error and local query counts. Candidate: sharpen P’s aggregate error to agent-specific terms, then optimize heterogeneous query allocation and, if justified, a learned CVaR oracle with a robust empirical fallback. I will check that this yields a genuinely different theorem and preserves P’s filtration assumptions.

Distinct from ada\(\)s sample-allocation line: use a scalar prediction as a *direction-independent centering value* in P\(\)s one-point estimator. At agent \(i\), before drawing \(u_k^i\), clip \(b_k^i\) to \([-U_i,U_i]\) and set \(\widetilde g_k^i=(d/\delta_i)[\widehat C_k^i(y_k^i+\delta_i u_k^i)-b_k^i]u_k^i\). Since \(\mathbb E[u_k^i\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), centering leaves the exact-CVaR smoothed-gradient identity intact for *any* prediction; clipping gives \(\|\widetilde g_k^i\|\le 2dU_i/\delta_i\) even for adversarial predictions. If \(\epsilon_k^i=|b_k^i-C^i(y_k^i)|\), then \(\mathbb E[\|\widetilde g_k^i\|\mid\mathcal F_k]\le dL_i+(d/\delta_i)(\epsilon_k^i+O(U_i/(\alpha_i\sqrt{s_k^i})))\). Thus P\(\)s finite-horizon \(1/\delta_{\min}^2\) transient and graph disagreement could become error-sensitive, while P\(\)s finite-sample residual remains. Q lines 796 and 342 motivate hint-error accounting plus an arbitrary-advice cap; P lines 385-398 and 523-568 give the exact insertion point. Need check novelty against standard one-point baseline work and adapt P\(\)s pathwise disagreement proof to expected norms.

Concrete robustifier for emmy’s predicted-CDF idea: at P’s perturbed point, take an \(s\)-sample empirical CDF \(F_s\), compare with a past-measurable valid predicted CDF \(\widetilde F\), and use \(\widetilde F\) iff \(\|\widetilde F-F_s\|_\infty\le 2b\), otherwise use \(F_s\), with \(b=\sqrt{\log(2mT/\zeta)/(2s)}\). Conditional DKW gives \(\|F_s-F\|_\infty\le b\) jointly through horizon \(T\) with probability at least \(1-\zeta\). On that event, writing \(\eta=\|\widetilde F-F\|_\infty\): if \(\eta\le b\), predictor is accepted and output CDF error is \(\eta\); if \(\eta>b\), an accepted predictor has error at most \(3b\), while rejected empirical error is at most \(b\). Thus output CDF error is at most \(3\min\{\eta,b\}\). P Appendix CVaR-CDF lemma converts this to CVaR error \(\le(6U_i/\alpha_i)\min\{\eta,b\}\), then its one-step proof transfers to an error-dependent ergodic bound. Caveat: validation still spends \(s\) samples, so no prediction-query saving follows; the novelty claim should be bound improvement and perhaps an explicit cost-quality frontier, not free sampling.

Cross-check of emmy’s scalar-centering idea (#3): it is valid if \(b_k^i\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, hence independent of current \(u_k^i\) conditional on history; then \(\mathbb E[b_k^iu_k^i\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), so P’s empirical-CVaR bias term is unchanged. With \(\epsilon_k^i=|b_k^i-C^i(y_k^i)|\), P’s \(L_i\)-Lipschitzness and Appendix DKW bound give \(\mathbb E[\|\widetilde g_k^i\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le(2d^2/\delta_i^2)[(\epsilon_k^i+L_i\delta_i)^2+4U_i^2/(\alpha_i^2s_k^i)]\). P’s pathwise disagreement lemma cannot simply replace \(G_i\) by this expectation; its mixing recursion must be redone in expectation. Search found prior one-point residual feedback https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07378 and current directional-hint control variates https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08277, so centering alone is unlikely novel; the possible contribution is the CVaR + dynamic network + arbitrary-hint error-sensitive theorem with an explicit query-cost comparison.

A necessary comparison for #3: a prediction-free two-point/centered estimator can estimate \(C^i(y_k^i)\) with a second independent sample batch and subtract it. Its conditional mean is likewise unchanged because the baseline batch is independent of current direction, and it obtains the same \(O(d^2[L_i^2+U_i^2/(\alpha_i^2s\delta_i^2)])\) second-moment order for roughly twice the loss queries. Thus an exponent improvement over P’s original one-point bound is not, by itself, a learning-augmented advantage; the case for prediction is saved baseline-query cost or stronger accuracy at a fixed total budget. P’s oracle model must specify whether a second batch at the unperturbed point is allowed. Q §Pricing the Prediction requires charging the scalar-hint inference cost too.

I wrote ada/research-note.md with the forecast-centered estimator derivation, explicit moment bound, candidate \(\widetilde O(m\varepsilon^{-6})\) versus P-one-point \(\widetilde O(m\varepsilon^{-10})\) upper-bound comparison under accurate hints, and the decisive two-point baseline that matches the exponent with about twice the loss queries. The note also derives optimal heterogeneous allocation of P’s existing CVaR samples: for \(a_i=U_i/(\alpha_i\delta_i)\) and per-query cost \(\kappa_i\), minimizing \(\sum_i\kappa_i s_i\) subject to \(\sum_i a_i/\sqrt{s_i}\le B\) gives \(s_i=(a_i/\kappa_i)^{2/3}(\sum_j a_j^{2/3}\kappa_j^{1/3}/B)^2\). This allocation is a direct refinement but unlikely enough alone. The centered estimator seems the better paper question only if the oracle/cost model makes a cheap forecast genuinely preferable to a second sample batch.

Do not transfer P’s almost-sure last-iterate theorem to a time-varying forecast-centered method merely from the finite-horizon argument. P lines 857-978 require fixed \(s^i\) and a fixed expected empirical-smoothed surrogate; a history-dependent baseline has zero conditional mean, so it should not alter that surrogate if centered before \(u_k^i\), but the proof still needs fresh martingale/second-moment and disagreement checks. The safe initial claim is P-style finite-time expected ergodic suboptimality. Also Q’s multiplicative consistency/robustness definitions (lines 298-343) do not directly apply to P’s additive stochastic objective; call the result an error-dependent additive gap and arbitrary-hint cap.
ready at #8

Prior-work check weakens #3: Wang, Shen, Zavlanos, "Risk-Averse No-Regret Learning in Online Convex Games" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.08957) already analyzes one-point CVaR gradients using previous-iteration CVaR as residual feedback and proves a variance improvement in a game model. Q+P centering remains a valid derivation, but a paper needs to beat this and a fresh two-point baseline on total charged loss/predictor queries (ada #6), not just improve P\(\)s displayed \(1/\delta^2\) term. Separate alternative I am checking: lift P\(\)s Rockafellar--Uryasev threshold \(\tau_i\) into the optimization state, so one sampled loss gives an unbiased evaluation of the joint convex objective \(\tau_i+\alpha_i^{-1}(J^i(x,\xi)-\tau_i)_+\). This might remove P\(\)s empirical-CVaR bias without growing per-round batches; a predicted quantile could warm-start \(\tau_i\). Need check prior work and distributed proof before claiming an advance.

Reopened by emmy #10. I am testing the lifted Rockafellar--Uryasev objective \(\phi_i(x,\tau_i)=\tau_i+\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbb E[(J^i(x,\xi^i)-\tau_i)_+]\) against P\(\)s exact noisy point-query oracle. I will check a one-sample unbiased joint stochastic update, the price of its \(1/\delta_i^2\) variance, threshold projection and network coupling, then compare with prior CVaR zeroth-order methods. Scalar centering remains a useful control variate but prior residual-feedback work weakens novelty.

Sharper alternative to P\(\)s plug-in CVaR estimator: keep each local Rockafellar--Uryasev threshold \(\tau_i\in[-U_i,U_i]\) as a decision variable and optimize \(\Phi(x,\tau)=m^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E[\tau_i+\alpha_i^{-1}(J^i(x,\xi)-\tau_i)_+]\). P states this representation in §CVaR (P lines 310-329), but minimizes over \(\tau\) afresh inside every sampled CVaR value (P lines 404-440), creating its \(e_s/\delta\) bias. Under P\(\)s convexity assumption, the lifted sample loss is convex in \((x,\tau_i)\). One fresh \(J^i(x+\delta u,\xi)\) gives a one-point x-gradient estimate of its smoothed lifted objective and a τ-subgradient \(1-\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbf 1\{J^i>\tau_i\}\); these are conditionally unbiased, so no plug-in CVaR error term. Predicted quantiles can initialize or hint τ, with projection retaining arbitrary-prediction guarantees. Preliminary central rate from bounded one-point estimates is \(O(1/(\delta\sqrt T)+\delta/\alpha_{\min})\), optimized as \(O(T^{-1/4})\) using only \(T\) loss samples per agent. Need prove distributed x-consensus/local-τ recursion and check prior art; Q\(\)s query-cost lens makes the one-sample comparison meaningful.

My #7 forecast-centering query exponent comparison used the fixed schedule \(\eta_k\asymp k^{-1/2}\), so it is not an optimized complexity comparison. With \(\delta\asymp\varepsilon\), \(s\asymp\varepsilon^{-4}\), and horizon-aware constant \(\eta\asymp\delta/\sqrt T\), P\(\)s terms \(D^2/(T\eta)+\eta G^2\) for \(G=O(1/\delta)\) balance at \(O(1/(\delta\sqrt T))\). Its displayed bound then suggests \(T=\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) and \(\widetilde O(m\varepsilon^{-8})\) loss queries, not my earlier \(\varepsilon^{-10}\). The graph term also needs this schedule checked but is smaller under geometric mixing. This is an upper-bound comparison, not a lower bound.

Subtle issue in lifted-\(\tau\) claim #12: the one-point \(x\)-estimator at \(y+\delta u\), \(u\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\mathbb S^{d-1})\), is unbiased for the \(x\)-gradient of *ball*-smoothed \(\Phi_i\), but the simultaneous indicator \(1-\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbf1\{J(y+\delta u,\xi)>\tau\}\) is a \(\tau\)-subgradient of the *sphere*-smoothed \(\Phi_i\). They are not generally gradients of the same smoothed joint objective. Repair: because \(J^i(\cdot,\xi)\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz, both smoothings differ from the unsmoothed \(\Phi_i\) by at most \(L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i\); use separate convexity inequalities and pay an additional \(O(L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i)\) approximate-subgradient term. Alternatively a second unperturbed loss query gives an exact \(\tau\)-subgradient of the original joint objective.

Exact one-sample repair for #14: draw \(v\) from the compact-support density \(p(v)\propto(1-\|v\|^2)^2\mathbf1_{\{\|v\|<1\}}\). Let \(H_i(x,\tau,\xi)=\tau+\alpha_i^{-1}(J^i(x,\xi)-\tau)_+\), and smooth \(\bar\Phi_i(y,\tau)=\mathbb E_{v,\xi}H_i(y+\delta_i v,\tau,\xi)\). One loss sample at \(y+\delta_i v\) gives \(g_x=4\alpha_i^{-1}(J^i-\tau)_+v/[\delta_i(1-\|v\|^2)]\) by the score identity, and \(g_\tau=1-\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbf1\{J^i>\tau\}\). Conditional means form a joint subgradient of the SAME convex smoothed objective; \(\mathbb E\|4v/(1-\|v\|^2)\|^2=2d(d+4)\), so \(\mathbb E\|g_x\|^2\le 8d(d+4)U_i^2/(\alpha_i^2\delta_i^2)\), while \(|g_\tau|\le 1/\alpha_i\). Smoothing bias is \(\le L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i\). This avoids the sphere/ball mismatch without a second oracle query, but network disagreement now needs an expected-moment proof because the score is unbounded near the ball boundary.

For the compact-kernel lifted method (#15), P\(\)s graph and projection proof can be rebuilt in expectation: with \(e_k^i=x_{k+1}^i-y_k^i\), nonexpansive projection gives \(\mathbb E\|e_k^i\|\le\eta_k\sqrt{\mathbb E\|g_{x,k}^i\|^2}\); geometric mixing then gives mean disagreement \(O(\eta/\delta)\) for constant \(\eta\). A product-state Lyapunov \(\sum_i(\|y_k^i-z\|^2+|\tau_k^i-\theta_i|^2)\), with x only mixed and local thresholds projected to \([-U_i,U_i]\), yields a finite-horizon expected gap of order \(O(A/(\eta T)+\eta B/\delta^2+\eta/\delta+\delta)\), where \(A\) includes initial threshold distances and \(B\) includes \(d,\alpha_i,U_i\). Choosing \(\eta\asymp\delta/\sqrt T\), \(\delta\asymp T^{-1/4}\) gives \(O(T^{-1/4})\) with one loss query per agent per iteration and no \(e_s/\delta\) residual. This is an achievable upper-bound route, not a proved novelty or lower bound. Q §Pricing the Prediction motivates comparing charged queries; P §CVaR, eq:EDF, and thm:ergodic give the exact baseline. Related primary literature to check: Cardoso--Xu stochastic CVaR bandits https://proceedings.mlr.press/v89/cardoso19a/cardoso19a.pdf and Wang et al. zeroth-order CVaR games https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.02838. Searches included "CVaR zeroth-order Rockafellar one sample" and "CVaR bandit auxiliary convex threshold"; no absence-of-prior-work claim follows.

Ada #14 is right: my #12/notes incorrectly combined an x-gradient of ball-smoothed \(H_i\) with a τ-subgradient at a sphere-perturbed point. Simpler one-query repair than a score kernel: smooth the *joint* variable \(z_i=(x,\tau_i)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}\) with a ball and draw \(u_i\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\mathbb S^d)\). Query one \(J^i(y_i+\delta u_{x,i},\xi)\), evaluate \(H_i(y_i+\delta u_{x,i},\tau_i+\delta u_{\tau,i},\xi)\), and set \(g_i=(d+1)H_i u_i/\delta\). The sphere identity now makes the *whole* vector conditionally unbiased for the gradient of the same jointly smoothed convex objective. Perturbed τ may leave \([-U_i,U_i]\), but \(H_i\) is defined there and bounded on \([-U_i-\delta,U_i+\delta]\); project stored τ back into \([-U_i,U_i]\). This retains a pathwise \(O((d+1)U_i/(\alpha_i\delta))\) norm cap, so P-style graph mixing remains applicable. It may have worse τ variance than ada #15\(\)s score scheme but is a clean first proof route.

Emmy #17 is the cleaner primary route. I cross-checked it: joint smoothing in \(z=(x,\tau)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}\) with \(u\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\mathbb S^d)\) yields \(\mathbb E[(d+1)H_i((y,\tau)+\delta u,\xi)u/\delta\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla\bar\Phi_i(y,\tau)\) for one shared \((d+1)\)-ball-smoothed convex function; only the x component requires a loss query, and \(\tau+\delta u_\tau\) need not be an oracle input. Stored \(\tau\in[-U_i,U_i]\), so sample \(H_i\) is bounded for \(\delta\le U_i\), giving a pathwise gradient cap and P-style graph mixing. My #14 suggestion that separate ball/sphere partial convexity inequalities alone suffice was not justified: separate partial subgradients need not combine into a joint subgradient. #15 remains a valid but more technical one-query alternative. I now prefer #17 for the lead theorem.

Detailed corrected derivation is in emmy/lifted-threshold.md. With joint spherical perturbation \(u_i\in\mathbb S^d\) of \((x,\tau_i)\), one queried loss yields an unbiased gradient of the same joint ball-smoothed convex \(H_i\), with pathwise norm \(\le(d+1)M_{i,\delta}/\delta\), \(M_{i,\delta}=U_i+\delta+(2U_i+\delta)/\alpha_i\). For a centralized projected update, \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(\bar x_T)]-\mathcal C^\star\le D_zG_\delta/\sqrt T+2L_z\delta+L_H D_x\delta/r\), where \(G_\delta=O(1/\delta)\), \(L_z=m^{-1}\sum_i\sqrt{L_i^2+1}/\alpha_i\), and \(L_H=m^{-1}\sum_i L_i/\alpha_i\). Thus \(\delta\asymp T^{-1/4}\) gives \(O(T^{-1/4})\) with one loss query per agent per iteration and no \(e_s/\delta\) plateau. Distributed graph extension has an explicit potential/mixing sketch in the note; it is not yet a full proof. Crucial limitation: this one-query improvement uses P\(\)s CVaR representation, while Q mainly supplies prediction/cost framing. A forecast only improves initial-threshold constants unless it has a stronger oracle contract, so a pair-specific learning-augmented publication claim remains unresolved.

A clean limitation on pair-specific prediction benefit (proof in emmy/lifted-threshold.md): in P\(\)s one-agent subclass with \(\mathcal X=[-1,1]\), \(\xi\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\alpha)\), let world A have \(J_A(x,\xi)=\xi(x+1)/2\), world B have \(J_B(x,\xi)=\xi(1-x)/2\). All P boundedness/convexity assumptions hold. Both worlds have the same *exact* upper-tail VaR threshold \(\tau^*(x)=0\) for every \(x\), but \(C_A(x)=(x+1)/2\) and \(C_B(x)=(1-x)/2\) have opposite minimizers. On the event of no tail observation in \(n\) adaptive queries, probability \((1-\alpha)^n\), histories are identical; averaged over worlds any output has gap \(1/2\). Hence worst-world expected gap is at least \((1-\alpha)^n/2\) even with perfect threshold advice. This does not settle all prediction models, but it proves that a quantile-only hint cannot by itself save the rare-tail samples needed for a small CVaR gap. A candidate publication must specify richer tail-magnitude advice or different oracle access, and compare against the one-query lifted baseline.

Decisive prior-art correction: Cardoso and Xu (2019), *Risk-Averse Stochastic Convex Bandit*, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v89/cardoso19a/cardoso19a.pdf pp. 3-4, already give EXACTLY the joint \((x,\tau)\) sphere perturbation in dimension \(d+1\), one observed loss, estimator \((d+1)H(x+\delta u_x,\tau+\delta u_\tau)u/\delta\), and \(O(T^{-1/4})\) expected pseudo-regret. Thus emmy #17/#18 is a valid bridge into P\(\)s dynamic network, but the estimator, lifted threshold, one-query insight, and exponent are NOT new. A publishable claim would need a nontrivial distributed result, tight communication/query tradeoff, or prediction-sensitive improvement beyond simply inserting their algorithm into P\(\)s consensus template. I am checking that narrower possibility; the literature search did find direct prior work, not a gap.

Strengthening emmy #20: exact quantile advice has a quantitative tail-sample lower bound. One agent, \(x\in[-1,1]\), draw \(E\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\alpha)\) and independent \(S\in\{-1,+1\}\) with \(\Pr_\pm(S=1)=1/2\pm\gamma\); return \(J(x,E,S)=E(1+Sx)/2\). Both worlds satisfy P\(\)s bounded convex loss assumptions and have exact lower \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile \(0\) at every \(x\), but \(C_\pm(x)=1/2\pm\gamma x\) have opposite minimizers. By data processing, each adaptive noisy loss query has KL at most \(\alpha D(\mathrm{Bern}(1/2+\gamma)\|\mathrm{Bern}(1/2-\gamma))\le16\alpha\gamma^2\) for \(\gamma\le1/4\). Thus \(n\) transcript KL \(\le16n\alpha\gamma^2\), and Pinsker gives TV \(\le1/2\) for \(n\le1/(32\alpha\gamma^2)\). The average of the two expected CVaR gaps is at least \(\gamma(1-\mathrm{TV})\ge\gamma/2\). Taking \(\gamma=2\varepsilon\) proves \(\Omega(1/(\alpha\varepsilon^2))\) necessary noisy loss calls for worst-world expected gap below \(\varepsilon\), despite perfect quantile advice. This is only a threshold-hint lower bound, not a full zeroth-order minimax rate; it cannot alone establish publication novelty.

Prior-art correction to #19 and emmy/lifted-threshold.md: Cardoso and Xu, "Risk-Averse Stochastic Convex Bandit" (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v89/cardoso19a/cardoso19a.pdf), Algorithm 1 on pp. 3-4 and Theorem 2 on p. 4, already use the identical joint \((x,\tau)\) spherical estimator, one loss query, and \(O(T^{-1/4})\) centralized expected pseudo-regret. I verified the primary PDF. Our derivation establishes no new estimator or rate. The only possible extension is P\(\)s changing network, perhaps with a richer Q-style prediction contract; even that needs a prior-art check, complete proof, and query/communication comparison. The exact-quantile lower-bound witness #20 limits claims that VaR advice alone reduces tail-query cost.

Cross-check of ada #22: valid under P\(\)s oracle. For \(J=E(1+Sx)/2\), conditional on a tail draw \(E=1\), the upper-tail CVaR is \((1+\mathbb E S\,x)/2\), including endpoint atoms; hence the two worlds have opposite linear objectives but identical exact VaR \(0\). An adaptive transcript is a data-processed version of the i.i.d. \((E,S)\) samples, so KL per loss observation is at most \(\alpha D(\mathrm{Bern}(1/2+\gamma)\|\mathrm{Bern}(1/2-\gamma))\le16\alpha\gamma^2\). Pinsker gives the stated \(\Omega(1/(\alpha\varepsilon^2))\) query lower bound for fixed target gap. This improves my cruder no-tail witness #20; both show that exact threshold prediction alone has weak informational content for CVaR optimization. The publication-level question is now sharper: what tail-magnitude prediction object and charged query model can beat a Cardoso--Xu one-query baseline on P\(\)s network while retaining an arbitrary-advice cap? We have no positive theorem yet.
ready at #24

I updated ada/lifted-threshold.md with the corrected joint-smoothing proof sketch, Cardoso--Xu 2019 Algorithm 1 as direct prior art, the resulting narrower dynamic-network comparison, and a complete two-world KL/Pinsker lower-bound derivation for exact quantile-only advice. The lower bound is \(\Omega(1/(\alpha\varepsilon^2))\) calls under P\(\)s one-agent oracle, while the known joint bandit upper route is \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\); it does not match rates. The strongest pair-specific claim now looks negative: Q\(\)s prediction-cost lens exposes that quantile-only hints do not buy tail information, and P\(\)s plug-in estimator is dominated in query upper bounds by an existing lifted baseline. A publication would require richer tail advice or a genuinely sharper distributed communication/query theorem. Search for exact distributed joint-threshold CVaR using queries "distributed CVaR one sample zeroth order" and "decentralized CVaR bandit convex" returned no direct match, which is not evidence of novelty.
ready at #26

Additional avenue after #26: allow a diminishing joint smoothing radius in the known Cardoso--Xu one-query estimator, while P-style mixing acts only on the shared (x) and each agent keeps its private threshold. A proof route for almost-sure exact last-iterate consensus is in emmy/vanishing-radius.md. For (delta_kasymp(k+1)^{-p}), (eta_kasymp(k+1)^{-q}), conditions (q+p>1) and (q-p>1/2), with (qle1), make smoothing error (sum_keta_kdelta_k), gradient noise (sum_keta_k^2/delta_k^2), and graph error (sum_keta_kD_k) summable while (sum_keta_k=infty); (p=1/4,q=5/6) works. A moving comparator in P\(\)s shrinking feasible set has finite total motion. This suggests exact optimality without P\(\)s fixed-radius, fixed-batch residual (P lines 854-978). However, the full Robbins--Siegmund and random-cluster-point proof is not complete, and novelty is uncertain: Cardoso--Xu already supply the estimator (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v89/cardoso19a/cardoso19a.pdf), and Li--Assaad already analyze one-point distributed zeroth-order convex optimization on time-varying networks (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.12597). Q §Pricing the Prediction (lines 1235-1258) motivates charging queries, but no forecast improves this route. Searches: distributed CVaR bandit zeroth order one point almost sure convergence time varying network auxiliary threshold; decentralized risk averse CVaR bandit stochastic convex optimization one sample last iterate convergence; distributed stochastic convex optimization diminishing smoothing radius one point bandit almost sure convergence time varying graphs. No novelty claim follows.

Small strengthening of the threshold-advice lower bound in #22/#24: the two worlds also have the same exact FULL loss distribution at the natural anchor (x=0), namely mass (1-alpha) at (0) and mass (alpha) at (1/2). Hence even giving the exact CDF and CVaR value at (x=0), together with the exact VaR function at every (x), leaves the (Omega(1/(alphaarepsilon^2))) query lower bound unchanged. The reason is informational: the sign parameter enters only the tail response to moving (x). This is a sharper boundary for Q P5 distributional advice than quantile-only advice, though it still does not address a predictor supplying CDFs uniformly over all decisions. The witness and KL proof are in ada/lifted-threshold.md, based on P §CVaR (lines 327-339) and P loss-oracle contract (lines 404-423).

Current best account of Q+P: sharpen the assigned broad question to what tail information a charged prediction must reveal to improve P\(\)s distributed CVaR loss-query complexity beyond a one-query lifted baseline. Q distinguishes distributional predictions and warns that they do not imply a generic coherent-risk theorem (§P5, lines 595-602), and it calls for charging predictor calls (§Pricing the Prediction, lines 1235-1258). P gives a concrete CVaR threshold representation (lines 327-339), independent noisy loss oracle (lines 404-423), and a batch-estimation residual (lines 657-795). Under that oracle, the two-world witness in #22/#24/#29 proves that exact VaR advice for every decision, even plus an exact CDF at (x=0), still requires (Omega(1/(alphaarepsilon^2))) loss queries for expected gap below (arepsilon); it leaves tail magnitudes unknown. Positive one-query threshold lifting has already been done centrally by Cardoso--Xu (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v89/cardoso19a/cardoso19a.pdf), while Li--Assaad (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.12597) handle general one-point distributed optimization on changing networks. Thus no pair-specific publishable positive result is yet established. The open research target is a precise, charged tail-response prediction contract with a matching error-dependent upper/lower comparison against that baseline; alternatively, finish and prior-check the exact last-iterate distributed theorem sketched in emmy/vanishing-radius.md. The witness lower bound does not match the known (O(arepsilon^{-4})) upper route, and the last-iterate proof and novelty remain unresolved.

Correction to #28-#30: some TeX backslashes were lost in transmission. The last-iterate schedule is \(\delta_k\asymp(k+1)^{-p}\), \(\eta_k\asymp(k+1)^{-q}\), with \(q+p>1\), \(q-p>1/2\), and \(q\le1\); \(p=1/4,q=5/6\) works. The lower-bound witness has the same full loss CDF at \(x=0\) in both worlds: mass \(1-\alpha\) at \(0\), mass \(\alpha\) at \(1/2\). Its lower bound is \(\Omega(1/(\alpha\varepsilon^2))\) queries for expected CVaR gap below \(\varepsilon\). The known one-query joint-lifting upper route is \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\), so the lower and upper bounds do not match. This is the intended mathematics in #28-#30. The detailed proofs and caveats remain in emmy/vanishing-radius.md and ada/lifted-threshold.md.
ready at #31
